name: TRON_LOG_LEVEL

rederive.audience_reason: It sets the amount of log output of every deployed TRON program, and a wrong name turns all log output off.
rederive.disagreement: Vague. Both inventory files say the accepted names and the result of an unknown name were 'not determined', and that the way spdlog combines logger level and sink level was not determined. spdlog v1.17.0 answers all three. (1) The accepted names are trace, debug, info, warning, error, critical and off, plus warn and err. The match is exact and case-sensitive. (2) Any other text, the empty text included, gives the level off. The process then writes no log message at all, not even errors. (3) SPDLOG_LEVEL changes only the logger level. The sinks keep the TRON_LOG_LEVEL level. The stricter of the two wins. Source: spdlog v1.17.0, read from a local build copy at /home/jhan/workspace/tron/gen/_deps/spdlog-src (its version.h reports 1.17.0). The checkout pins v1.17.0 at cmake/versions.cmake:5 but does not hold the spdlog source. The default (debug) and the read time agree.
rederive.effect: Sets the lowest message level that TRON writes. The level is applied to the log file sink, to the stderr sink and to the default logger (src/system/spdlog.cpp:47, :50, :55).
rederive.empty_value: The empty text is not a level name, so the level is off. No message is written to stderr or to the log file.
rederive.how_to_check: none found. No log line prints the level in effect. A debug line such as the per-card 'caps { ... }' line (src/pos/device.cpp:337) appears only at debug or trace.
rederive.interactions: SPDLOG_LEVEL is applied after it (src/system/spdlog.cpp:60). In spdlog v1.17.0, load_env_levels changes only the level of the logger. The two sinks keep the level from TRON_LOG_LEVEL, and a message must pass both the logger level and the sink level. So the stricter of the two variables wins. SPDLOG_LEVEL can hide more messages but cannot show more than TRON_LOG_LEVEL allows. Example: trace output needs TRON_LOG_LEVEL=trace. SPDLOG_LEVEL=trace alone leaves the sinks at debug. Only the first call of init_logging reads the variable (static flag at src/system/spdlog.cpp:36-37). No command-line flag sets the log level (no set_level call outside src/system/spdlog.cpp in src/ and h/). The pos_fake startup does not call init_logging. Several tests read the same name with their own getenv (for example t/t_scheduler.cpp:35).
rederive.invalid_value: Every text that is not one of the listed names gives the level off (spdlog from_str returns level::off). Examples: INFO, Debug, verbose, 'info ' with a space, 3. No warning is printed. With the level off, neither stderr nor the log file gets any message. This includes error messages and the message of a failed TRON_ASSERT, which is written with spdlog::error (h/common/assert.hpp:60-62).
rederive.name: TRON_LOG_LEVEL

entries.name: TRON_MAX_MAIN_HELPERS
entries.notes: Main helpers are thread pool workers that help the main thread with non-attention work; the other pool workers run attention. The variable is read each time a model state is constructed. The value must not be below the minimum (TRON_MIN_MAIN_HELPERS or its default); otherwise TRON_ASSERT_LE at h/tron/models/model.hpp:1616 aborts the process. On a pool of 16 or more workers the default minimum is 1, so the value 0 alone aborts there. The source comment says 0 can be used to avoid deadlock bugs (h/tron/models/model.hpp:71).

rederive.audience_reason: Performance tuning of rinzler and runtron: it limits how the worker threads are split between main work and attention.
rederive.default: Unset: half of the app pool workers, by integer division (h/tron/models/model.hpp:82). The app pool has the number of app CPUs minus 1 workers (h/tron/threading.hpp:754-755).
rederive.effect: Sets the upper limit of main helpers in each forward pass. Main helpers are app pool workers that help the main thread with the non-attention work. The other pool workers run attention. The value 0 turns main helpers off (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2375-2376).
rederive.empty_value: Parses as 0. The rule for 0 then applies: main helpers are off, and the process aborts if the minimum is above 0.
rederive.how_to_check: No log line or stat prints the value. If min is above max the abort message is 'TRON_ASSERT((min_main_helpers) <= (max_main_helpers)): Expected min_main_helpers <= max_main_helpers, but got <min> > <max>.' (h/tron/models/model.hpp:1616, h/common/assert.hpp:82-83). Indirect check: with TRON_ATTN_STATS on, the attention report holds n_attn_workers_min and n_attn_workers_max (h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp:768). The helpers of a pass are the pool workers minus the attention workers (h/tron/plugins/llama.hpp:657).
rederive.interactions: TRON_MIN_MAIN_HELPERS must not be above this value. On a pool of 16 or more workers the default minimum is 1 (h/tron/models/model.hpp:75-76), so TRON_MAX_MAIN_HELPERS=0 alone aborts there. Set TRON_MIN_MAIN_HELPERS=0 as well. The count of one pass is min(parallelism the model plugin reports, min(max, max(min, n))) (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2413-2415). With pay_for_determinism the fixed split (pool workers times 2, divided by 7) is still limited by this value (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2377-2382 and :2414). The comment at h/tron/models/model.hpp:2360-2365 says a change of the split changes the attention plan and the exact logits. The code does not limit the value to the pool size. The value is read again for each scheduler that is built. No command-line flag sets it. rinzler_proxy and rinzler_mock do not run this read: they have their own get_scheduler (src/tron/scheduler/proxy.cpp:87, src/tron/scheduler/mock.cpp:67).
rederive.invalid_value: Non-numeric text parses as 0. A negative number wraps to a very large unsigned value, so the variable then sets no upper limit. If the result is below the minimum (TRON_MIN_MAIN_HELPERS or its default), TRON_ASSERT_LE at h/tron/models/model.hpp:1616 aborts the process when the scheduler is built, which is at model load. TRON_ASSERT is active in every build type (h/common/assert.hpp:3-5 and :69-75). It logs the message, logs 'Aborting.' and calls std::abort (h/common/assert.hpp:57-63).

On a value of 0 or below the abort message is 'TRON_ASSERT((timescale) > (0.0f)): Expected timescale > 0.0f, but got <value> <= 0.'
rederive.interactions: The value is also the divisor in the pull factor exp(-prior_strength / timescale) of TRON_SPEEDOMETER_PRIOR_STRENGTH (h/tron/threading.hpp:531). The speed estimates split the attention work between the attention workers (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2422-2446). With pay_for_determinism the estimates are not used (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2426-2431). The estimator is updated once for each attention plan, so once per forward pass (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2424 and :2678). No command-line flag sets it.
rederive.invalid_value: Non-numeric text parses as 0.0. A value of 0 or below fails TRON_ASSERT_GT at h/tron/threading.hpp:528 and the process aborts when the thread pool is built. TRON_ASSERT is active in every build type (h/common/assert.hpp:3-5 and :69-75). It logs the message, logs 'Aborting.' and calls std::abort (h/common/assert.hpp:57-63).

entries.notes: Read each time a Python fallback tokenizer is created. That happens when the model directory has no tokenizer.json, when the Rust tokenizer fails to load, or when USE_PYTHON_TOKENIZER or VALIDATE_TOKENIZERS is enabled. If the program does not exist, a TRON_ASSERT aborts the process with the text 'Python tokenizer script ... not found; run in the tron source directory or set TRON_TOKENIZE_PY.' (src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp:462). The command is '<program> -n <model directory>' plus -v or -e. It is started with popen, so it runs through a shell and the child process inherits the whole environment. Set outside this area at flake.nix:578 and bin/dice-lsf-runner:1408. The comment at packaging/tron-host/90-rinzler-host.conf:11 says the packaged unit keeps the working directory /opt/positron for this relative path.

rederive.audience_reason: A path that a deployed rinzler needs when it uses the Python fallback tokenizer; a wrong path aborts the process.
rederive.default: Unset: the relative path bin/tokenize_py (src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp:453). The process resolves it against its current working directory.
rederive.effect: Selects the program that the Python fallback tokenizer starts as a child process to read the vocabulary and to encode text. The command is '<program> -n <model directory>' plus an option, started with popen (src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp:460 and :467-469).
rederive.how_to_check: Warning log line each time a Python fallback tokenizer is built: 'Falling back to slow tokenizer script <path>' (src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp:461). The path in that line is the value in effect.
rederive.interactions: The variable matters only when a Python fallback tokenizer is built. That happens in three cases: the model directory has no tokenizer.json or the Rust tokenizer fails to load (src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp:1891-1903); USE_PYTHON_TOKENIZER is set and is not the text false (:2197-2204); VALIDATE_TOKENIZERS is set and is not the text false (:2193-2196 and :1940). The path is put into a shell command line without quotes. Outside product code: the make rule for gen/tokenize_py copies the file that the variable names when IN_NIX_SHELL is set (GNUmakefile:549-557); flake.nix:578 and :1924 set it in the Nix shells; bin/dice-lsf-runner:1408 sets it for test jobs. No command-line flag sets it.
rederive.invalid_value: If the path does not exist, TRON_ASSERT at src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp:462-465 aborts the process with 'Python tokenizer script <path> not found; run in the tron source directory or set TRON_TOKENIZE_PY.' The abort is not an exception, so the try block in make_python_tokenizer does not catch it (src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp:1923-1929). If the program exists but fails, the constructor throws 'Python tokenizer subprocess failed ...' (src/rinzler/tokenizers.cpp:476-480).
rederive.name: TRON_TOKENIZE_PY
